newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian metalworkers unions call for more strikes.
newsitem.headline: Italian metalworkers unions call for more strikes.

text.p: Italian trade unions representing 1.5 million engineering and metalworkers in a bitter pay dispute said on Monday they had called 10 hours of strikes to press their demands.
The announcement by the three unions included a previously announced four-hour stoppage set for December 13, when other sectors are due also to halt work in the metalworkers' support.
A statement by the unions said the other six hours would be decided at factory level.
The unions have previously held two eight-hour strikes on September 27 and last Friday, when tens of thousands of their members also staged a mass demonstration in Rome.
The unions are protesting a refusal by management to compensate workers fully for higher-than-expected inflation in the past contractual period.

In cash terms, unions want a 262,000 lire ($175) rise in their monthly pay packets, of which 97,000 is to cover the overrun in inflation between 1994 and 1996. Employers have offered 195,000 lire of which just 30,000 is for inflation.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government has said that if the employers' association, Federmeccanica, does not return to the bargaining table by November 28 it will intervene in the dispute to seek a settlement.
